charts.title: Bitcoin Market Overview
charts.description: An orientation chart pairing Bitcoin's price with realized price, the 200-week moving average, hashrate and the 32x thermocap band.

charts.title: Bitcoin Metcalfe Model
charts.description: The Metcalfe model values a network in proportion to the square of its users, estimated here from address counts above four balance thresholds.

charts.title: Bitcoin Mining Electricity Cost
charts.description: Bitcoin's electricity cost of production, the power expense of mining one coin, modelled across tariffs from $0.03 to $0.07 per kWh.

charts.title: Bitcoin Power Law Model
charts.description: The power law model fits Bitcoin's price to a straight line on a log-log scale against time, treating growth as a function of network age.

charts.title: Bitcoin Price
charts.description: Bitcoin's price and market capitalisation in US dollars, from the earliest exchange data through the most recent daily close.

charts.title: Bitcoin Price Moving Averages
charts.description: Bitcoin's price against its 7, 50 and 200-day and 200-week moving averages, with the multiple of price to the 200-day average.

charts.title: Bitcoin Production Price
charts.description: Bitcoin's cost of production, combining the power expense of mining a coin with the Hayes cost-of-production network price.

charts.title: Bitcoin Satoshis Per Dollar
charts.description: Satoshis per dollar expresses Bitcoin's price inverted: how many of the smallest units, one hundred-millionth of a coin, one dollar buys.

charts.title: Bitcoin Stock To Flow Price
charts.description: Stock-to-flow values Bitcoin by the ratio of existing supply to annual new issuance, a scarcity measure that steps up at each halving.

charts.title: Bitcoin Volatility
charts.description: Bitcoin's realised volatility, the annualised standard deviation of daily returns, measured over rolling 30-day and 180-day windows.

charts.title: Bitcoin Delta Cap
charts.description: Delta cap is realized cap minus average cap, a long-term valuation floor derived from the difference between on-chain and lifetime average pricing.

charts.title: Bitcoin NUPL (Net Unrealized Profit/Loss)
charts.description: Net Unrealized Profit/Loss is the total paper gain or loss held across all circulating supply, expressed as a share of market capitalisation.

charts.title: Bitcoin NVT Price
charts.description: NVT price values Bitcoin from the value settled on-chain, applying the network-value-to-transactions ratio in reverse to imply a fair price.

charts.title: Bitcoin Price On-Chain Value
charts.description: A composite of Bitcoin's on-chain valuation models: realized price and its cohorts, the Hayes network price, and the 200-week moving average.

charts.title: Bitcoin Realized Price
charts.description: Realized price is the average on-chain acquisition cost of all circulating coins, valuing each at the price it last moved rather than today's.

charts.title: Bitcoin Thermocap Multiple
charts.description: Thermocap is the cumulative value paid to miners since genesis; thermocap price divides it by supply to give a security-spend valuation floor.

charts.title: Bitcoin vs Gold Market Cap
charts.description: Bitcoin's market capitalisation set against gold and silver, with gold broken into jewellery, private investment, official holdings and industrial use.

charts.title: Bitcoin vs M0 Money Supply
charts.description: Bitcoin's market capitalisation set against the M0 base money supply of nine major economies, from the United States and China to Australia.

charts.title: Bitcoin vs Mega-Cap Equities
charts.description: Bitcoin's market capitalisation set against the world's largest listed companies, spanning technology, energy, finance and Bitcoin-linked equities.

charts.title: Bitcoin Relative Valuation
charts.description: Bitcoin's price if its market capitalisation matched each of ten reference assets, from silver and gold to Apple, NVIDIA and US base money.

charts.title: Bitcoin Relative Valuation: Big Tech
charts.description: Bitcoin's price if its market capitalisation matched a mega-cap technology company: Meta, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft or Apple.

charts.title: Bitcoin Relative Valuation: Financials
charts.description: Bitcoin's price if its market capitalisation matched a major financial or payments firm: Berkshire Hathaway, JPMorgan, Visa, PayPal or Block.

charts.title: Bitcoin Relative Valuation: Gold and Silver
charts.description: Bitcoin's price if its market capitalisation matched silver or gold, with gold split into private investment, official holdings and the total market.

charts.title: Bitcoin Relative Valuation: M0 Money Supply
charts.description: Bitcoin's price if its market capitalisation matched the M0 base money supply of the United Kingdom, Japan, China, the United States or the EU.

charts.title: Bitcoin Relative Valuation: Sector Leaders
charts.description: Bitcoin's price if its market capitalisation matched a cross-sector leader: Tesla, Eli Lilly, Saudi Aramco or SpaceX.

charts.title: Bitcoin Relative Valuation: Semiconductors
charts.description: Bitcoin's price if its market capitalisation matched a leading semiconductor firm: NVIDIA, Broadcom, TSMC, Samsung Electronics or Micron.

charts.title: Bitcoin Drawdowns From All-Time High
charts.description: Bitcoin's drawdowns from each all-time high, aligned at the peak so the depth and duration of all five cycles can be compared directly.

charts.title: Bitcoin Index Performance Since Halving
charts.description: Bitcoin's price performance indexed from each halving, aligning the 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024 eras from the day issuance last halved.

charts.title: Bitcoin Price Performance Since Cycle Low
charts.description: Bitcoin's price performance indexed from each cycle low, aligning six market cycles from the day the bear market bottomed.

charts.title: Bitcoin 4-Year CAGR
charts.description: Bitcoin's four-year compound annual growth rate, the annualised return an investor would have earned over any rolling four-year holding period.

charts.title: Bitcoin 4-Year CAGR vs Other Assets
charts.description: Four-year compound annual growth rates for Bitcoin and eight benchmarks, covering equities, technology, financials, gold, bonds, the dollar and miners.

charts.title: Bitcoin MTD Return vs Other Assets
charts.description: Month-to-date returns for Bitcoin and eight benchmarks, covering equities, technology, financials, gold, bonds, the dollar and Bitcoin miners.

charts.title: Bitcoin MTD Returns by Year
charts.description: Bitcoin's month-to-date return for every calendar year since 2014, shown as a daily percentage alongside the median and average across years.

charts.title: Bitcoin MTD Returns, Indexed
charts.description: Bitcoin's month-to-date return path for every year since 2014, indexed to the current month so each year's shape can be compared day by day.

charts.title: Bitcoin YTD Return vs 16 Benchmarks
charts.description: Year-to-date returns for Bitcoin and sixteen benchmarks: US and international equities, sector funds, commodities, bonds and Bitcoin-linked stocks.

charts.title: Bitcoin YTD Return vs Other Assets
charts.description: Year-to-date returns for Bitcoin and eight benchmarks, covering equities, technology, financials, gold, bonds, the dollar and Bitcoin miners.

charts.title: Bitcoin YTD Returns by Year
charts.description: Bitcoin's year-to-date return for every calendar year since 2014, shown as a daily percentage alongside the median and average across years.

charts.title: Bitcoin YTD Returns, Indexed
charts.description: Bitcoin's year-to-date return path for every year since 2014, indexed to the current year so each year's shape can be compared day by day.

charts.title: Bitcoin Year-Over-Year Return
charts.description: Bitcoin's year-over-year return, the percentage change in price against the same date twelve months earlier, plotted against price itself.

charts.title: Bitcoin 1+ Year Supply
charts.description: One-year active supply is the share of circulating Bitcoin that has moved at least once in the past year, the mirror of long-dormant coins.

charts.title: Bitcoin Macro Supply
charts.description: Bitcoin's supply split by liquidity and holding period, separating liquid from illiquid coins and short-term from long-term holder balances.

charts.title: Bitcoin Supply & Daily Issuance
charts.description: Bitcoin's circulating supply against daily new issuance, the coins created by each block subsidy, smoothed over 30-day and 365-day windows.

charts.title: Bitcoin Supply Age Distribution
charts.description: Bitcoin's supply grouped by how recently each coin last moved, from under one month to over ten years, showing the distribution of holding periods.

charts.title: Bitcoin Active Addresses
charts.description: Active addresses count the distinct Bitcoin addresses sending or receiving in a day, a measure of network use smoothed over 30 and 365 days.

charts.title: Bitcoin Address Balance Distribution
charts.description: The number of Bitcoin addresses holding at least a given balance, across thirteen thresholds from a single satoshi to ten thousand coins.

charts.title: Bitcoin Transaction Fees
charts.description: Total Bitcoin transaction fees paid to miners each day in US dollars, the portion of miner revenue that does not come from the block subsidy.

charts.title: Bitcoin Transaction Volume
charts.description: Bitcoin transaction volume is the total value settled on-chain each day, smoothed over 30-day and 365-day windows to show the underlying trend.

charts.title: Bitcoin Transactions
charts.description: The number of Bitcoin transactions confirmed each day, with 30-day and 365-day moving averages to separate short-term noise from the trend.

charts.title: Bitcoin Hash Price
charts.description: Hash price is miner revenue per terahash per second per day, the dollar income a unit of mining hardware earns and the core measure of mining economics.

charts.title: Bitcoin Hash Ribbons
charts.description: Hash ribbons compare Bitcoin's 30-day and 60-day hashrate averages; their crossover marks miner capitulation and the recovery that follows.

charts.title: Bitcoin Hashrate
charts.description: Hashrate is the total computing power securing the Bitcoin network, smoothed over 30-day and 365-day windows to see through short-term variance.

charts.title: Bitcoin Miner Revenue
charts.description: Total daily miner revenue in US dollars, the block subsidy plus transaction fees, smoothed over 30-day and 365-day windows.

charts.title: Bitcoin Network Difficulty
charts.description: Mining difficulty is the target the network adjusts roughly every two weeks to hold block times near ten minutes as hashrate changes.

charts.title: Bitcoin Price & Hashrate
charts.description: Bitcoin's price against the total hashrate securing the network, with 30-day and 365-day averages of the computing power committed to mining.

charts.title: Bitcoin Puell Multiple
charts.description: The Puell Multiple divides the daily dollar value of newly issued coins by its own 365-day average, measuring miner revenue against its norm.

charts.title: Bitcoin Days Destroyed, Supply-Adjusted
charts.description: Bitcoin Days Destroyed weights each coin moved by how long it sat still; adjusting for circulating supply makes the measure comparable across eras.

charts.title: Bitcoin HODL Bank & Reserve Risk
charts.description: HODL Bank accumulates the opportunity cost borne by long-term holders; reserve risk divides price by it to gauge conviction against price.

charts.title: Bitcoin SOPR (Spent Output Profit Ratio)
charts.description: Spent Output Profit Ratio compares the value of coins when spent to their value when acquired, with 1.0 marking the aggregate break-even line.

charts.title: Bitcoin Supply in Profit vs Loss
charts.description: The share of circulating Bitcoin last moved below and above the current price, splitting total supply into coins held in profit and in loss.
